```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(p8105.datasets)
```

## Problem 1
### Data cleaning and description

```{r}
data("ny_noaa")

noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )
```

The original dataset contains `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations and
`r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables from `r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` weather
stations in New York. Each observation represents weather measurements
for one station on one date. The data include precipitation, snowfall,
snow depth, and maximum and minimum temperatures.

```{r}
noaa_df |>
  summarise(
    across(
      c(prcp, snow, snwd, tmax, tmin),
      ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_percent"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Variable", "Missing (%)")
  )
```
Both maximum and minimum temperatures are missing for 43.7% of observations.
Snow depth is missing for 22.8%, snowfall for 14.7%, and precipitation
for 5.6%. Therefore, summaries and plots based on observed values may
not fully represent all stations and dates.

### Most common snowfall values

```{r}
noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Snowfall (mm)", "Number of observations")
  )
```
The most common snowfall value is 0 mm, with 2,008,508 observations,
because most station-days have no snowfall. Other common values include
25, 13, and 51 mm. These values are approximately 1, 0.5, and 2 inches,
suggesting that measurements originally recorded in inches were
converted to millimeters and rounded.

### Average maximum temperature in January and July

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
noaa_monthly =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

noaa_monthly |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature by Station and Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)"
  )
```
Average maximum temperatures are much higher in July than in January.
January also shows larger year-to-year fluctuations. Many stations
follow similar patterns across years, suggesting shared regional
weather patterns. There are some possible outliers, including a July
average near 14°C around 1988, well below the other stations. Unusual
values may reflect local conditions, incomplete observations, or
recording errors and would require further investigation.

### Temperature relationship and snowfall distributions

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
temp_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin_2d(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum versus Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  )

snow_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Snowfall by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)
  )

temp_plot / snow_plot
```
Maximum and minimum temperatures show a strong positive relationship:
days with higher minimum temperatures generally also have higher
maximum temperatures. A few observations have extreme temperatures,
and some appear to have maximum temperatures below minimum
temperatures, suggesting possible recording errors.

For snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 mm, the
distributions are similar across years. The median is approximately
25 mm in each year, and the middle 50% of observations generally fall
between about 13 and 51 mm. Some years, such as 2006, have a smaller
interquartile range. There is no clear long-term trend in these
conditional snowfall distributions.
